# `Q-12-10` — Listing Markdown Re-parse Diagnostics

> Re-parsing the markdown produced by the listing template
> surfaced one or more diagnostics.

## What this means

A listing renders in two steps. First, Quarto runs the listing
template (a built-in or a custom doctemplate) over the listing's
items and produces a string of markdown. Then it parses that
markdown back into an AST so the result can be spliced into the
host document.

If the second parse surfaces diagnostics, this diagnostic fires.
The message includes how many diagnostics the re-parse produced
and the title of the first one, so you can find the underlying
issue.

- When the re-parse **succeeds** with diagnostics (for example,
  raw HTML written by a custom template), it is a **warning** and
  the listing renders.
- When the re-parse **fails**, the listing is skipped and it is an
  **error**: a page that silently ships without its listing is
  easy to miss.

## Why this happens

Item metadata does not cause it: a listing writes each item's
`title`, `subtitle` and `description` back as markdown, with their
formatting kept and any markdown-significant text escaped. A title
such as `Fix \_scope` or ``About `<anonymous>` frames`` renders in
the listing as it does on its own page.

The usual trigger is a **custom template that produces
syntactically invalid output**: an unterminated fence, an
unclosed `_` or `*` in the template's own text, or a
`$variable$` interpolated where markdown does not expect it.

## How to fix

Inspect the first diagnostic the message mentions. Its error
code (`Q-2-*`) and message point at what the re-parser found
broken. Then trace it back to the custom template.
